The first official print alone controls; later revisions do not."},{"kind":"text","text":"The Census economic-indicator calendar explicitly schedules the June 2026 Advance Report on Durable Goods for July 27, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. EDT, verifying the ledger resolution date rather than inferring it from monthly cadence."},{"kind":"tool","tool":"official.lookup","call":"Fetch the latest Census M3 May 2026 Advance Table 2 defense capital-goods inventory row.","result":"The official seasonally adjusted preliminary values were May 2026 28,257 million, revised April 2026 28,161 million, and March 2026 28,022 million; May rose 0.3%."},{"kind":"tool","tool":"official.lookup","call":"Fetch the Census January 2026 Advance Table 2 defense capital-goods inventory history.","result":"The official seasonally adjusted values shown were January 2026 27,820 million, December 2025 27,668 million, and November 2025 27,738 million."},{"kind":"tool","tool":"official.lookup","call":"Fetch first-print defense capital-goods inventories from the February, March, and April 2026 Census advance releases.","result":"The preliminary seasonally adjusted prints were February 2026 27,877 million, March 2026 28,088 million, and April 2026 28,121 million."},{"kind":"text","text":"Outside view/base rate: the seven-month first-print reference class from November 2025 through May 2026 is 27.738, 27.668, 27.820, 27.877, 28.088, 28.121, and 28.257 billion. Six monthly changes average +0.0865 billion and are positive in five of six months, favoring another moderate increase over pure level persistence."},{"kind":"text","text":"Level is anchored at May's 28.257 billion. Momentum contributes about +0.087 billion from the mean monthly change. No identified one-off warrants a large adjustment; the policy/production mechanism is gradual accumulation in long-cycle defense manufacturing, so the combined estimate is rounded to 28.350 billion."},{"kind":"math","text":"Prior/update/interval: persistence-plus-drift prior using the seven first-print observations from November 2025-May 2026; successive changes are -0.070, +0.152, +0.057, +0.211, +0.033, and +0.136 billion. Their mean is +0.0865 and sample sigma = 0.101 billion. Point = 28.257 + 0.0865 = 28.3435, rounded to 28.35. The normal 80% half-width is 1.28*sigma = 1.28*0.101 = 0.129 billion, giving 28.35 ± 0.13 = [28.22, 28.48]."},{"kind":"text","text":"Upside risk comes from unusually rapid accumulation tied to aircraft, missile, ship, or communications production and would land above the interval if June adds more than about 0.22 billion. Downside risk is a drawdown, delivery-driven liquidation, or noisy seasonal adjustment; a fall of more than about 0.04 billion from May would land below the interval. Either would be outside the interval and falsify the smooth-accumulation reference class."},{"kind":"forecast","point":28.35,"ciLow":28.22,"ciHigh":28.48}]}
